# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Aug 7, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on refining the SDM refund policy, enhancing documentation clarity, and improving CI test efficiency. Significant progress was made in addressing sequencer starvation and resolving metrics port collisions in the ZK dispute game.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### SDM Policy Refinement and Sequencer Performance
The SDM refund policy was isolated behind a test-only fixture, removing it from public production binaries while maintaining generic post-execution policy hooks and verifier support ([#22289](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22289)). Additionally, the sequencer now runs on its own goroutine, eliminating starvation caused by the shared event loop and preventing block production from competing with derivation ([#22241](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22241)).

### Documentation Improvements and Accessibility
Several documentation issues were addressed to improve clarity and navigation. This included fixing unreachable root links, dead in-tree links, and mis-archived snap-sync guides ([#22317](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22317)). Colliding frontmatter page titles were disambiguated ([#22314](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22314)), the Kona node actor list and extension mechanism were corrected ([#22313](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22313)), and a new "Choose how to run your chain" fork page was added ([#22312](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22312)). Stale op-reth OP Stack run pages were also retired ([#22316](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22316)).

### CI/CD and Testing Enhancements
Test jobs were sharded by historical timing and parallelism was widened to improve CI efficiency ([#22202](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22202)). A metrics port collision in the `kona-sp1-proposer` was resolved, fixing a flaking test related to concurrent challenged games ([#22300](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22300)). The `l2.follow.source.rpc-timeout` flag was also properly registered in `op-node` ([#22297](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22297)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- [#22332](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22332) [DO NOT MERGE] CI baseline probe for v7.0.0 cherry-picks
- [#22331](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22331) op-deployer: activate Karst at genesis by default (cherry-pick of #21633)
- [#22330](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22330) Lagoon hardfork rename (cherry-pick of #21105)
- [#22329](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22329) nuts: declare activation-block extra gas in the bundle schema
- [#22328](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22328) contracts-bedrock: Super ZK Dispute Game Internal Review Remediations
- [#22327](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22327) rust: dev-based ci profile with line-table debug info (measurement probe)
- [#22326](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22326) rust: dev-based ci profile with full debug info (measurement probe)
- [#22324](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22324) ci: probe the ci profile build on the 16GB class (measurement probe)
- [#22323](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22323) rust: re-add debug-assertions to the ci profile (measurement probe)
- [#22322](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22322) ci: front-load mise tool installs in the setup pipeline
- [#22321](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22321) op-devstack: retry tx-in-block reads that race canonical head flips
- [#22319](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22319) docs: replace the notices Archive sidebar group with an archive index

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Sequencer Performance and Derivation Issues Resolved
Long-standing issues related to sequencer starvation and block building delays during L1 batch derivation have been closed. This includes addressing the problem where the sequencer's FCU w/attr call could be delayed, causing late block production ([#19263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19263)). The general issue of sequencer and derivation thread contention/starvation in `op-node`'s single-threaded event loop has also been resolved ([#22232](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22232)).

### Post-Execution Transaction Validation and Tooling Updates
A latent Go↔Rust divergence where the post-execution (0x7D) transaction payload was not validated on decode has been closed. Both `op-node` and Kona now treat `PostExecTxs` as opaque bytes during derivation, with further validation being the EL's responsibility ([#21961](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21961)). Additionally, the milestone for `op-deployer` and Tooling Runbook, which introduced changes to `op-deployer` and new requirements for `intent.json`, has been completed ([#22114](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22114)).

### Test Flakiness Addressed
A flaking test, `TestProposerDefendsMultipleChallengedGamesConcurrently`, which experienced `kona-sp1-proposer` metrics port collisions, has been resolved ([#22299](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22299)).

## NEW ISSUES

### Sequencer Stability and Deadlock Concerns
New issues highlight potential stability problems within the sequencer. One concern is that the `op-node` sequencer's `Stop` function can block indefinitely while waiting for a head that may never arrive ([#22318](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22318)). Another issue points out that the sequencer compensates the seal deadline with a static constant instead of the measured seal duration, which could lead to inefficiencies ([#22320](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22320)).

### Supernode Cross-Chain Safety Issues
A critical issue has been identified where the `op-supernode`'s cross-safe mechanism can wedge after an invalid-message replacement, particularly when a local-safe on one chain stalls ([#22325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22325)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Conductor System Coverage and Flaky Test Resolution
Discussions on [#21902](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21902) and [#22094](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22094) indicate that PR [#22244](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22244) has been merged, closing both issues. This PR ports user-visible conductor behaviors to focused acceptance tests and removes superseded `op-e2e` coverage, addressing the flaky `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` test. The underlying `op-conductor` availability bug exposed by the flaky test is now tracked separately in a core-team issue, as the PR mitigates the reproducer but does not fix the product-level deadlock.

### Supernode Flakiness and Invalid Message Replacement
Issue [#22234](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22234) discusses the flakiness of `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`. A root cause has been identified as a race in the test's final assertions, where `AssertTxInBlock` (a by-number read against the canonical head) can transiently disagree with `Reached(eth.Safe, N)` (which checks the safe label number). This leads to failures when the light CL sequences a divergent branch while the follow-source loop reorgs the EL onto the upstream branch. A fix is proposed to replace the single-shot assertions with a retrying check that polls until the canonical block at N contains the transaction. A separate, high-priority issue ([#22325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22325)) has been created to investigate a genuine stall where the supernode's cross-safe head wedges after an invalid-message replacement, indicating a potential supervisor/cross-safety issue rather than just a test flakiness. A draft PR ([#22321](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22321)) is up to fix the first signature of the flake by retrying `AwaitTxInBlock`/`AwaitTxNotInBlock` DSL checks.
